output_text:
name: python-observability
description: Python patterns for structured logging, Prometheus metrics, distributed tracing, correlation IDs, dashboards, and production debugging.

Use JSON logs with consistent fields in production; human-readable logs may be used locally. Track latency, traffic, errors, and saturation at every service boundary. Thread one unique ID through all logs/spans for each request. Keep metric label values bounded. Unbounded labels (like user IDs) explode storage costs.

Use `structlog` with `structlog.contextvars.merge_contextvars`, `structlog.processors.add_log_level`, `structlog.processors.TimeStamper(fmt="iso")`, `structlog.processors.StackInfoRenderer()`, `structlog.processors.format_exc_info`, and `structlog.processors.JSONRenderer()`; configure JSON output and standard filtering/correlation fields. Use `ContextVar` and `X-Correlation-ID`; generate an ID at ingress, bind it, return it, and propagate it via `httpx.AsyncClient` outbound headers.

Use `prometheus_client` `Counter`, `Histogram`, and `Gauge` for `http_request_duration_seconds`, `http_requests_total`, `http_errors_total`, and `db_connection_pool_used`; instrument endpoints and time operations with `time.perf_counter()`.

Avoid labels with unbounded values to prevent metric explosion.
REQUEST_COUNT.labels(method="GET", user_id=user.id)  # Don't do this!
REQUEST_COUNT.labels(method="GET", endpoint="/users", status="200")

Never log expected behavior at `ERROR`. A user entering a wrong password is `INFO`, not `ERROR`.

Use OpenTelemetry `TracerProvider`, `BatchSpanProcessor`, `OTLPSpanExporter`, `trace.set_tracer_provider`, and `tracer.start_as_current_span`; check https://opentelemetry.io/docs/languages/python/.

Use appropriate levels: `DEBUG` diagnostics, `INFO` operations, `WARNING` recoverable anomalies, `ERROR` failures. Include user ID, request ID, and operation name; separate observability from business logic; test logs/metric
